title: Binary Vandermonde matrix of points
statement: Let $k,n,ell$ be natural numbers with $ell \ne 0$, and let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n$ be points in the degree-$\ell$ extension field of $\mathbb{F}_2$. The binary Vandermonde matrix has rows indexed by $0,\ldots,(k-1)\ell$ and columns indexed by the points: its first row consists of $1$'s, and each remaining row is the binary encoding of the corresponding coordinate of $\alpha_j^{q+1}$, where the row is indexed by a pair $(q,i)$ as specified by the Vandermonde row indexing.
hypotheses_covered: $\alpha$ assigns a degree-$\ell$ binary extension-field element to each of $n$ indices
caveat: The row-to-pair indexing equivalence and the binary extension encoding are not defined in the supplied upstream definitions, so their exact mathematical conventions cannot be stated self-containedly.
